title: Multislice-Based Quantitative Convergent-Beam Electron Diffraction and the Interrogation of Chemical Bonds and Point Defects Associated with Nanostructures in "Real" Materials
content: Unlike multislice ptychography, quantitative convergent-beam electron diffraction (QCBED) assumes the structure of the scattering volume as known (meaning that phase retrieval is not necessary). QCBED fine-tunes parameters associated with the assumed structure by fitting a calculated CBED pattern to an experimental one. It operates in a range of specimen thicknesses where the CBED patterns contain a highly detailed intensity distribution as a function of scattering angle, making QCBED sufficiently constrained to allow the refinement of chemical bonding-sensitive structure factors (Fourier coefficients of the crystal potential,V(r), / electron density, ρ(r)) to levels of accuracy and precision that permit electron distributions in chemical bonds to be mapped reliably [1, 2].
